messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We're building backend for a helpdesk SaaS for businesses and their customers.
Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.
Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.
Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

The owner needs help. Add an `agent` role and let admins invite other admins or agents:

```http
POST /api/v1/invitations

{"invitation":{"email":"sam@example.test","role":"agent"}}
```

Return an `invitation` and email a link to `/accept-invitation?account=acme&token=TOKEN` on the
frontend. Let admins list and inspect invitations, resend them with `POST /invitations/:id/resend`,
and revoke them with `DELETE /invitations/:id`. Track pending, accepted, revoked, and expired
invitations. Don't create competing invitations or let customer registration take a pending invite's email.
List invitations by ID ascending.

The acceptance screen uses `POST /invitation_previews` with
`{"invitation_preview":{"token":"TOKEN"}}` to show the invited email, role, business name, subdomain,
and expiry inside `invitation_preview`. Then it submits:

```http
POST /api/v1/invitation_acceptances

{"invitation_acceptance":{"token":"TOKEN","name":"Sam","password":"my-team-password"}}
```

Return `user` and `account`; Sam can sign in without another verification email.

Admins also need `GET /users`, `GET /users/:id`, and `PATCH /users/:id`. Include `suspended` on users
and support `{"user":{"suspended":true}}`. Suspension revokes sessions and clears assignments.
Don't let admins suspend the last active admin. Filter users by role or suspension, and invitations
by status. `GET /staff` supplies active staff choices for assignment controls.
List users and staff by ID ascending.

Staff can assign tickets with `{"ticket":{"assignee_id":12}}` or clear them with null. Include
`assignee_id` and the assignee's ID/name on tickets. Both admins and agents can work on the business's
tickets, but only admins manage people.

Add private notes through the existing comment input, for example
`{"ticket":{"comment":{"body":"Checking this with billing.","public":false}}}`.
Internal activity must not change the customer-facing request.


You can execute bash commands and edit files to implement the necessary changes.

module HelpdeskConfig
  DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL = "http://localhost:3001"
  DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM = "support@example.test"

  module_function

  def frontend_url
    (ENV["HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL"].presence || DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL).sub(%r{/+\z}, "")
  end

  def frontend_origin
    uri = URI.parse(frontend_url)
    if uri.scheme && uri.host

      "#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}#{port_part}"
    else
      frontend_url
    end
  rescue URI::InvalidURIError
    frontend_url
  end

  def mail_from

  end

    "#{frontend_url}/verify-email?account=#{CGI.escape(account.subdomain)}&token=#{CGI.escape(token)}"
  end

  def reset_password_url(account:, token:)

  ROLES = %w[admin agent customer].freeze
  STAFF_ROLES = %w[admin agent].freeze

  belongs_to :account

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :email_verification_tokens, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :password_reset_tokens, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :comments, foreign_key: :author_id, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :requested_tickets, class_name: "Ticket", foreign_key: :requester_id, dependent: :destroy

  has_secure_password

  normalizes :name, with: ->(name) { name.to_s.strip }
  normalizes :email, with: ->(email) { email.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true
  validates :email,
    presence: true,
    format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP, allow_blank: true },
    uniqueness: { scope: :account_id, case_sensitive: false }
  validates :role, presence: true, inclusion: { in: ROLES }

  before_save :sync_email_verified_at

  def owner?
    account.present? && account.owner_id == id
  end

  def staff?
    STAFF_ROLES.include?(role)
  end

  def admin?
    role == "admin"
  end

  def agent?
    role == "agent"
  end

  def customer?
    role == "customer"

      email_verification_tokens.create!(

        expires_at: 24.hours.from_now
      )
    end
  end

      email_verification_tokens.delete_all

    end

    transaction do
      self.password = new_password
      save!
      sessions.delete_all
      password_reset_tokens.delete_all
    end
  end

class User < ApplicationRecord
  ROLES = %w[admin agent customer].freeze
  STAFF_ROLES = %w[admin agent].freeze

  belongs_to :account

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :email_verification_tokens, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :password_reset_tokens, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :comments, foreign_key: :author_id, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :requested_tickets, class_name: "Ticket", foreign_key: :requester_id, dependent: :destroy

  has_secure_password

  normalizes :name, with: ->(name) { name.to_s.strip }
  normalizes :email, with: ->(email) { email.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true
  validates :email,
    presence: true,
    format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP, allow_blank: true },
    uniqueness: { scope: :account_id, case_sensitive: false }
  validates :role, presence: true, inclusion: { in: ROLES }

  before_save :sync_email_verified_at

    account.present? && account.owner_id == id
  end

    STAFF_ROLES.include?(role)
  end

  def admin?

  def agent?

  end

  def customer?
    role == "customer"
  end

      )

require "digest"

module TokenDigestable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    attr_reader :token

    before_validation :generate_token_digest, on: :create
  end

  class_methods do
    def digest_token(raw_token)
      Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw_token.to_s)
    end

    def find_by_raw_token(raw_token)
      return nil if raw_token.blank?

      find_by(token_digest: digest_token(raw_token))
    end
  end

  private

  def generate_token_digest
    return if token_digest.present?

    @token = SecureRandom.alphanumeric(48)
    self.token_digest = self.class.digest_token(@token)
  end

class Account < ApplicationRecord
  CANCELLATION_RETENTION_PERIOD = 90.days
  SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT = /\A[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?\z/

  belongs_to :owner, class_name: "User", optional: true

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :email_verification_tokens, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :password_reset_tokens, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :comments, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :tickets, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :users, dependent: :destroy

  before_destroy :clear_owner_reference, prepend: true

  normalizes :name, with: ->(name) { name.to_s.strip }
  normalizes :subdomain, with: ->(subdomain) { subdomain.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true
  validates :subdomain,
    presence: true,
    length: { maximum: 63 },
    format: { with: SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT, allow_blank: true },
    uniqueness: { case_sensitive: false }

  scope :active, -> { where(cancelled_at: nil) }
  scope :cancelled, -> { where.not(cancelled_at: nil) }
  scope :purgeable, -> { where("cancelled_at <= ?", CANCELLATION_RETENTION_PERIOD.ago) }

  def self.purge_expired_cancelled_accounts!
    purged_count = 0
    purgeable.find_each do |account|
      account.destroy!
      purged_count += 1
    end
    purged_count
  end

  def active?
    cancelled_at.nil?
  end

  def cancelled?
    cancelled_at.present?
  end

  def cancellation_expired?
    cancelled? && cancelled_at <= CANCELLATION_RETENTION_PERIOD.ago
  end

  def reactivable?
    cancelled? && !cancellation_expired?
  end

  def cancel!
    transaction do
      update!(cancelled_at: Time.current)
      sessions.delete_all
    end
  end

  def reactivate!
    update!(cancelled_at: nil)
  end

  def portal_json
    {
      name: name,
      subdomain: subdomain
    }
  end

  def api_json
    {
      id: id,
      name: name,
      subdomain: subdomain,
      owner_id: owner_id,
      cancelled_at: cancelled_at,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  private

  def clear_owner_reference
    update_column(:owner_id, nil) if owner_id.present?
  end
end

require "digest"
require "securerandom"

module TokenDigestable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    attr_reader :token

    before_validation :generate_token_digest, on: :create
  end

  class_methods do
    def digest_token(raw_token)
      Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw_token.to_s)
    end

    def find_by_raw_token(raw_token)
      return nil if raw_token.blank?

      find_by(token_digest: digest_token(raw_token))
    end
  end

  private

  def generate_token_digest
    return if token_digest.present?

    @token = SecureRandom.alphanumeric(48)
    self.token_digest = self.class.digest_token(@token)
  end
end

        headers: {
          "Origin" => "http://localhost:3001",
          "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "corsco"
        }
      assert_response :ok
      assert_equal "http://localhost:3001", response.headers["Access-Control-Allow-Origin"]
    end
  end

    post "/api/v1/account/create",

  end

    end
  end

    headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer #{token}" if token.present?
    headers
  end

  def extract_token_from_last_email
    mail = ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last
    assert_not_nil mail, "Expected an email to have been sent"
    token = mail.body.decoded[/token=([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)/, 1]
    assert token.present?, "Expected token in email body"
    token
  end

          admin: {
            name: owner_name,
            email: owner_email,
            password: password
          }
        }
      },

      patch "/api/v1/me", params: { user: { name: "Blocked" } }, headers: headers_for("acme", owner_recovery_token), as: :json
      assert_response :forbidden

      # Owner reactivates the account
      post "/api/v1/account/reactivate", headers: headers_for("acme", owner_recovery_token), as: :json
      assert_response :ok
      assert_nil response.parsed_body.dig("account", "cancelled_at")
      assert account.reload.active?

      # Ordinary business access works again immediately
      get "/api/v1/portal", headers: headers_for("acme")
      assert_response :ok
      get "/api/v1/account", headers: headers_for("acme", owner_recovery_token)
      assert_response :ok
      get "/api/v1/me", headers: headers_for("acme", owner_recovery_token)
      assert_response :ok

      # Non-owner can sign in again
      login(subdomain: "acme", email: "sam@acme.test", password: "sam-password")
      assert_response :created
    end
  end

  test "cannot reactivate or sign in after 90 days of cancellation" do
    create_verified_account_with_owner(subdomain: "expiredco")

    login(subdomain: "expiredco", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
    owner_token = response.parsed_body.dig("session", "token")

    post "/api/v1/account/cancel", headers: headers_for("expiredco", owner_token), as: :json
    assert_response :ok

    # Sign in at day 89 to hold a session across the 90-day mark
    recovery_token = nil
    travel 89.days do
      login(subdomain: "expiredco", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
      assert_response :created
      recovery_token = response.parsed_body.dig("session", "token")
    end

    travel 90.days + 1.second do
      # Cannot sign in past 90 days
      login(subdomain: "expiredco", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
      assert_response :forbidden

      # Even with pre-existing recovery session, reactivation past 90 days is rejected
      post "/api/v1/account/reactivate", headers: headers_for("expiredco", recovery_token), as: :json

Okay, here's what's running through my mind as I analyze this:  AHA! That `test/integration/business_signup_and_auth_test.rb` is the key. Lines 325-333 are highlighting a crucial inconsistency. Specifically, I'm thinking about the way we're handling account verification, password resets, and now invitation previews. I'm seeing that when we try to confirm an ACME token against a different account, Globex, we get an unprocessable entity response, like with `EmailVerificationsController#confirm` and `PasswordResetsController#confirm`. The email links for verification and password reset all use the format `/accept-invitation?account=acme&token=TOKEN`. And critically, they *all* expect the `X-Helpdesk-Account: acme` header.

The mental wheels are turning now. What happens with `POST /api/v1/invitation_previews` and `POST /api/v1/invitation_acceptances`? If I send the right `X-Helpdesk-Account` header, it works; if I send the wrong one, I get a 422, just like with the email verifications and password resets.  If I omit the header entirely, I get a 404, when I might expect a 400. That's a good place to start!

The pattern is becoming clear. The `account=acme` in the URLs is there because *every* tenant-scoped endpoint requires the `X-Helpdesk-Account` header. That's why we see it in `/verify-email`, `/reset-password`, and now, apparently, `/accept-invitation`.  Endpoints without the header trigger a 400 Bad Request.  If the account is cancelled, we see a 403 Forbidden. This is all 100% consistent with the `EmailVerificationsController` and `PasswordResetsController` behavior.

Now, let's refocus on the `invitation_preview` JSON. The prompt emphasizes that the preview will show "the invited email, role, business name, subdomain, and expiry inside `invitation_preview`."  I'm drilling down on the exact keys: is it `email`, `role`, and what about the business name? Is it a flat `account_name` key? Is it an nested `account` object containing `name` and `subdomain`? A Rails developer's style is the key to the pattern! I'm thinking about how someone would structure the `Invitation#preview_json`.  Looking at `Account#portal_json` and `Ticket#ticket_json`, I'm seeing the two main options.  The Invitation belongs to the account. Is `Invitation#preview_json` flat? First off, we're dealing with role-based access control (RBAC): admins, agents, and customers. Admins get the keys to manage users and invitations, while agents work on tickets and can pull active staff. Customers are, as always, locked out of anything sensitive. We need to respect the staff's needs while maintaining the customer's workflow.

Next, suspension: This requires a boolean `suspended` column on the `users` table. The implications of suspension are significant: a suspended user *cannot* sign in (session creation should immediately reject), any existing sessions are revoked, and they are prevented from resetting their passwords or verifying their email address during their suspension. Crucially, on suspension, ticket assignments must be cleared. This will involve an `update_all` query on the `tickets` table, but we MUST make absolutely sure this internal activity doesn't update `customer_updated_at`. Also, we need to add a check to stop someone from suspending the last active admin. This "active admin" check demands that they are not suspended, not an unverified, and *must* be an admin. We also need to think about how updating roles works and ensure that changing roles to prevent this restriction can not happen.

Now, filtering and listing users are next. We'll be using query parameters to filter by role and suspension status. Invalid parameters should return an HTTP 422. We also want an endpoint to list active staff for assignment controls that includes the `suspended` and `verified` states, and we'll have to consider how to handle staff creation by invitation or manually within the API.

Ticket assignment is up next. We'll add an `assignee_id` foreign key. The system will need to ensure that the `assignee_id` corresponds to an active, staff member of the *same* account and must not be a customer. Invalid `assignee_id`s should return a 422. When any customer-visible activity (public comment, status change, or customer updates a request) happens, both timestamps must be updated. require "digest"
require "securerandom"

module TokenDigestable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    attr_reader :token

    before_validation :generate_token_digest, on: :create
  end

  class_methods do
    def digest_token(raw_token)
      Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw_token.to_s)
    end

    def find_by_raw_token(raw_token)
      return nil if raw_token.blank?

      find_by(token_digest: digest_token(raw_token))
    end
  end

  def regenerate_token_digest!
    @token = SecureRandom.alphanumeric(48)
    self.token_digest = self.class.digest_token(@token)
    @token
  end

  private

  def generate_token_digest
    return if token_digest.present?

    regenerate_token_digest!
  end
end
EOF

class Invitation < ApplicationRecord
  include TokenDigestable

  EXPIRATION_PERIOD = 7.days
  ROLES = User::STAFF_ROLES
  STATUSES = %w[pending accepted revoked expired].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :invited_by, class_name: "User", optional: true

  normalizes :email, with: ->(email) { email.to_s.strip.downcase }

  before_validation :set_default_expiration, on: :create

  validates :email,
    presence: true,
    format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP, allow_blank: true }
  validates :role, presence: true, inclusion: { in: ROLES }
  validates :token_digest, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :expires_at, presence: true
  validate :invited_by_belongs_to_account

  scope :by_id, -> { order(id: :asc) }
  scope :pending, -> { where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil).where("expires_at > ?", Time.current) }
  scope :accepted, -> { where.not(accepted_at: nil) }
  scope :revoked, -> { where(accepted_at: nil).where.not(revoked_at: nil) }
  scope :expired, -> { where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil).where("expires_at <= ?", Time.current) }

  def self.with_status(status)
    case status
    when "pending" then pending
    when "accepted" then accepted
    when "revoked" then revoked
    when "expired" then expired
    else none
    end
  end

  def accepted?
    accepted_at.present?
  end

  def revoked?
    !accepted? && revoked_at.present?
  end

  def expired?
    !accepted? && !revoked? && expires_at <= Time.current
  end

  def pending?
    !accepted? && !revoked? && expires_at > Time.current
  end

  def status
    if accepted?
      "accepted"
    elsif revoked?
      "revoked"
    elsif expired?
      "expired"
    else
      "pending"
    end
  end

  def api_json
    {
      id: id,
      email: email,
      role: role,
      status: status,
      invited_by_id: invited_by_id,
      expires_at: expires_at,
      accepted_at: accepted_at,
      revoked_at: revoked_at,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  def preview_json

      role: role,
      account_name: account.name,
      subdomain: account.subdomain,
      account: account.portal_json,
      expires_at: expires_at

  scope :cancelled, -> { where.not(cancelled_at: nil) }
  scope :purgeable, -> { where("cancelled_at <= ?", CANCELLATION_RETENTION_PERIOD.ago) }

  def self.purge_expired_cancelled_accounts!
    purged_count = 0
    purgeable.find_each do |account|
      account.destroy!
      purged_count += 1
    end
    purged_count
  end

    cancelled_at.nil?
  end

    cancelled_at.present?
  end

  def cancellation_expired?
    cancelled? && cancelled_at <= CANCELLATION_RETENTION_PERIOD.ago
  end

  def reactivable?
    cancelled? && !cancellation_expired?
  end

  def cancel!
    transaction do
      update!(cancelled_at: Time.current)
      sessions.delete_all
    end
  end

  def reactivate!
    update!(cancelled_at: nil)
  end

module Api
  module V1
    class BaseController < ApplicationController
      DEFAULT_PAGE = 1
      DEFAULT_PER_PAGE = 25

      attr_reader :current_account, :current_user, :current_session

      rescue_from ActionController::ParameterMissing do |exception|
        render json: { error: exception.message }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end

      rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid do |exception|
        render_validation_errors(exception.record)
      end

      rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique do
        render json: { error: "Record already exists" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end

      rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound do
        render json: { error: "Not found" }, status: :not_found
      end

      def route_not_found
        render json: { error: "Not found" }, status: :not_found
      end

      private

      def require_hash_param(key)
        value = params.require(key)
        return value if value.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters) || value.is_a?(Hash)

        raise ActionController::ParameterMissing, key
      end

      def require_account!
        subdomain = request.headers["X-Helpdesk-Account"].to_s.strip.downcase
        if subdomain.blank?
          render json: { error: "Missing X-Helpdesk-Account header" }, status: :bad_request
          return
        end

        @current_account = Account.find_by(subdomain: subdomain)
        return if @current_account

        render json: { error: "Account not found" }, status: :not_found
      end

      def authenticate_user!
        token = bearer_token
        if token.blank?
          render json: { error: "Unauthorized" }, status: :unauthorized
          return
        end

        session = current_account.sessions.includes(:user).find_by_raw_token(token)
        if session.nil? || session.user.nil? || session.user.account_id != current_account.id || session.user.suspended?
          render json: { error: "Unauthorized" }, status: :unauthorized
          return
        end

        @current_session = session
        @current_user = session.user
      end

      def ensure_account_active!
        return if current_account&.active?

        render json: { error: "Account is cancelled" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def require_owner!
        return if current_user&.owner?

        render json: { error: "Forbidden" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def require_admin!
        return if current_user&.admin?

        render json: { error: "Forbidden" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def require_staff!
        return if current_user&.staff?

        render json: { error: "Forbidden" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def require_customer!
        return if current_user&.customer?

        render json: { error: "Forbidden" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def parse_boolean(value)
        case value
        when true, "true" then true
        when false, "false" then false
        else :invalid
        end
      end

      def paginate(scope, includes: nil)
        raw_page = params[:page]
        page = (raw_page.is_a?(String) || raw_page.is_a?(Numeric)) && raw_page.present? ? raw_page.to_i : DEFAULT_PAGE
        page = DEFAULT_PAGE if page < 1

        raw_per_page = params[:per_page]
        per_page = (raw_per_page.is_a?(String) || raw_per_page.is_a?(Numeric)) && raw_per_page.present? ? raw_per_page.to_i : DEFAULT_PER_PAGE
        per_page = DEFAULT_PER_PAGE if per_page < 1

        count = scope.count
        total_pages = (count.to_f / per_page).ceil

        offset = (page - 1) * per_page
        records = if offset >= count
          []
        else
          page_scope = scope.offset(offset).limit(per_page)
          page_scope = page_scope.includes(includes) if includes
          page_scope.to_a
        end

        next_page = page < total_pages ? page + 1 : nil
        previous_page = if page > 1 && total_pages > 0
          [ page - 1, total_pages ].min
        else
          nil
        end

        [
          records,
          {
            count: count,
            page: page,
            per_page: per_page,
            next_page: next_page,
            previous_page: previous_page
          }
        ]
      end

      def bearer_token
        header = request.headers["Authorization"].to_s
        match = header.match(/\ABearer\s+(\S+)\z/i)
        match && match[1]
      end

      def render_validation_errors(record)
        render json: {
          error: record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence,
          errors: record.errors.to_hash(true)
        }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end
  end
end

module Api
  module V1
    class InvitationsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_account!
      before_action :authenticate_user!
      before_action :ensure_account_active!
      before_action :require_admin!
      before_action :set_invitation, only: %i[show resend destroy]

      def index
        scope = current_account.invitations

        if params.key?(:status) && params[:status].to_s != ""
          status = params[:status].is_a?(String) ? params[:status].strip : nil
          unless Invitation::STATUSES.include?(status)
            return render json: {
              error: "Status is not included in the list",
              errors: { status: [ "Status is not included in the list" ] }
            }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end
          scope = scope.with_status(status)
        end

        scope = scope.by_id
        records, meta = paginate(scope)

        render json: {
          invitations: records.map(&:api_json),
          **meta
        }, status: :ok
      end

      def show
        render json: { invitation: @invitation.api_json }, status: :ok
      end

      def create
        inv_params = require_hash_param(:invitation)
        raw_email = inv_params[:email]
        raw_role = inv_params[:role]

        invitation = current_account.invitations.new(
          invited_by: current_user,
          email: raw_email.is_a?(String) ? raw_email : nil,
          role: raw_role.is_a?(String) ? raw_role : nil
        )

        current_account.with_lock do
          invitation.valid?
          if invitation.email.present? && invitation.errors[:email].empty?
            if current_account.users.exists?(email: invitation.email)
              invitation.errors.add(:email, "has already been taken")
            elsif current_account.invitations.pending.exists?(email: invitation.email)
              invitation.errors.add(:email, "already has a pending invitation")
            end
          end

          if invitation.errors.any?
            return render_validation_errors(invitation)
          end

          invitation.save!
        end

        UserMailer.invitation(invitation: invitation, token: invitation.token).deliver_now

        render json: { invitation: invitation.api_json }, status: :created
      end

      def resend
        current_account.with_lock do
          @invitation.reload

          if @invitation.accepted?
            return render json: {
              error: "Accepted invitation cannot be resent",
              errors: { status: [ "Accepted invitation cannot be resent" ] }
            }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end

          if @invitation.revoked?
            return render json: {
              error: "Revoked invitation cannot be resent",
              errors: { status: [ "Revoked invitation cannot be resent" ] }
            }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end

          if current_account.users.exists?(email: @invitation.email)
            return render json: {
              error: "Email has already been taken",
              errors: { email: [ "Email has already been taken" ] }
            }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end

          if current_account.invitations.pending.where.not(id: @invitation.id).exists?(email: @invitation.email)
            return render json: {
              error: "Email already has a pending invitation",
              errors: { email: [ "Email already has a pending invitation" ] }
            }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end

          @invitation.regenerate_token_digest!
          @invitation.expires_at = Invitation::EXPIRATION_PERIOD.from_now
          @invitation.save!
        end

        UserMailer.invitation(invitation: @invitation, token: @invitation.token).deliver_now

        render json: { invitation: @invitation.api_json }, status: :ok
      end

      def destroy
        current_account.with_lock do
          @invitation.reload

          unless @invitation.pending?
            message = if @invitation.accepted?
              "Accepted invitation cannot be revoked"
            elsif @invitation.revoked?
              "Invitation has already been revoked"
            else
              "Expired invitation cannot be revoked"
            end
            return render json: {
              error: message,
              errors: { status: [ message ] }
            }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end

          @invitation.update!(revoked_at: Time.current)
        end

        render json: { invitation: @invitation.api_json }, status: :ok
      end

        if params.key?(:suspended) && params[:suspended].to_s != ""
          suspended_val = parse_boolean(params[:suspended])
          if suspended_val == :invalid
            return render json: {
              error: "Suspended is not included in the list",
              errors: { suspended: [ "Suspended is not included in the list" ] }
            }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end
          scope = scope.where(suspended: suspended_val)
        end

          **meta
        }, status: :ok
      end

      end

        user_attrs = require_hash_param(:user)
        has_suspended = user_attrs.key?(:suspended)
        has_role = user_attrs.key?(:role)
        has_name = user_attrs.key?(:name)

        unless has_suspended || has_role || has_name
          return render json: {
            error: "User attributes can't be blank",
            errors: { base: [ "User attributes can't be blank" ] }
          }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        current_account.with_lock do
          @user.reload
          was_active_admin = @user.admin? && !@user.suspended? && @user.verified?
          custom_errors = {}

          if has_name
            raw_name = user_attrs[:name]
            @user.name = raw_name.is_a?(String) ? raw_name : nil
          end

          if has_role
            raw_role = user_attrs[:role]
            new_role = raw_role.is_a?(String) ? raw_role : nil
            if @user.customer? && new_role != "customer"
              custom_errors[:role] = [ "Customer role cannot be changed" ]
            elsif @user.staff? && !User::STAFF_ROLES.include?(new_role)
              custom_errors[:role] = [ "Role is not included in the list" ]
            elsif @user.owner? && new_role != "admin"
              custom_errors[:role] = [ "Account owner must remain an admin" ]
            else
              @user.role = new_role
            end
          end

          if has_suspended
            suspended_val = parse_boolean(user_attrs[:suspended])
            if suspended_val == :invalid
              @user.suspended = nil
            else
              @user.suspended = suspended_val
            end
          end

          @user.valid?
          combined_errors = @user.errors.to_hash(true)
          all_messages = @user.errors.full_messages.dup

          custom_errors.each do |field, msgs|
            combined_errors[field] = (combined_errors[field] || []) + msgs
            all_messages.concat(msgs)
          end

          will_be_active_admin = @user.admin? && @user.suspended == false && @user.verified?
          if combined_errors.empty? && was_active_admin && !will_be_active_admin
            other_active_admins = current_account.users
              .where(role: "admin", suspended: false, verified: true)
              .where.not(id: @user.id)
              .exists?

            unless other_active_admins
              msg = "Cannot suspend or demote the last active admin"
              err_key = has_suspended && @user.suspended ? :suspended : :role
              combined_errors[err_key] = [ msg ]
              all_messages << msg
            end
          end

          if combined_errors.any?
            return render json: {
              error: all_messages.to_sentence,
              errors: combined_errors
            }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end

          @user.save!

          if @user.suspended?
            @user.sessions.delete_all
            @user.password_reset_tokens.delete_all
            current_account.tickets.where(assignee_id: @user.id).update_all(assignee_id: nil)
          end
        end

        render json: { user: @user.api_json }, status: :ok
      end

            end

            public_value = if comment_attrs.key?(:public)

      )

          params: { invitation_preview: { token: expired_token } },
          headers: account_headers("acme"),
          as: :json

          params: { invitation_acceptance: { token: expired_token, name: "Late", password: "pw" } },

          as: :json
        assert_response :unprocessable_entity

        delete "/api/v1/invitations/#{expired_inv_id}", headers: account_headers("acme", owner_token), as: :json

        # Inspect expired invite
        get "/api/v1/invitations/#{expired_inv_id}", headers: account_headers("acme", owner_token)
        assert_response :ok
        assert_equal "expired", response.parsed_body.dig("invitation", "status")

        # Create a pending admin invite
        post "/api/v1/invitations",
          params: { invitation: { email: "pat@example.test", role: "admin" } },
          headers: account_headers("acme", owner_token),
          as: :json
        assert_response :created
        pending_inv_id = response.parsed_body.dig("invitation", "id")

        # List all invitations: ordered by ID ascending
        get "/api/v1/invitations", headers: account_headers("acme", owner_token)
        assert_response :ok
        all_invs = response.parsed_body.fetch("invitations")
        assert_equal [ sam_inv_id, revoked_inv_id, expired_inv_id, pending_inv_id ], all_invs.map { |i| i["id"] }
        assert_equal %w[accepted revoked expired pending], all_invs.map { |i| i["status"] }

        # Filter invitations by each status
        {
          "pending" => [ pending_inv_id ],
          "accepted" => [ sam_inv_id ],
          "revoked" => [ revoked_inv_id ],
          "expired" => [ expired_inv_id ]
        }.each do |st, expected_ids|
          get "/api/v1/invitations", params: { status: st }, headers: account_headers("acme", owner_token)
          assert_response :ok
          assert_equal expected_ids, response.parsed_body.fetch("invitations").map { |i| i["id"] }
          assert_equal expected_ids.size, response.parsed_body["count"]
        end

        # Invalid status filter returns 422
        get "/api/v1/invitations", params: { status: "unknown" }, headers: account_headers("acme", owner_token)
        assert_response :unprocessable_entity

        # Resending an expired invite makes it pending again with a working token
        post "/api/v1/invitations/#{expired_inv_id}/resend", headers: account_headers("acme", owner_token), as: :json
        assert_response :ok
        assert_equal "pending", response.parsed_body.dig("invitation", "status")
        revived_token = extract_invitation_token_from_last_email(
          expected_path: "https://app.helpdesk.test/accept-invitation",
          expected_account: "acme"
        )
        post "/api/v1/invitation_previews",
          params: { invitation_preview: { token: revived_token } },
          headers: account_headers("acme"),
          as: :json
        assert_response :ok
      end
    end
  end

  test "people management, suspension rules, staff choices, ticket assignments, and private notes isolation" do

    sam_token = response.parsed_body.dig("session", "token")

    avery, avery_token = register_and_verify_customer(subdomain: "acme", name: "Avery Customer", email: "avery@example.test")

    # Only admins manage people: agent and customer are forbidden on /invitations and /users
    [ sam_token, avery_token ].each do |tok|

      post "/api/v1/invitations",

      get "/api/v1/users/#{jo.id}", headers: account_headers("acme", tok)
      assert_response :forbidden

      patch "/api/v1/users/#{sam.id}",
        params: { user: { suspended: true } },
        headers: account_headers("acme", tok),
        as: :json
      assert_response :forbidden
    end

    # Customer cannot access /staff, but BOTH admin and agent CAN access /staff (ordered by ID asc)
    get "/api/v1/staff", headers: account_headers("acme", avery_token)
    assert_response :forbidden

    [ jo_token, sam_token ].each do |tok|

      assert_equal [ "Jo Admin", "Sam Agent" ], staff_list.map { |s| s["name"] }
      assert_equal %w[admin agent], staff_list.map { |s| s["role"] }
    end

    # Cannot suspend the last active admin (Jo is currently the only admin, even though Sam is an active agent)
    patch "/api/v1/users/#{jo.id}",
      params: { user: { suspended: true } },
      headers: account_headers("acme", jo_token),
      as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_equal false, jo.reload.suspended?

    # Customer opens two requests so we can verify ordering and request payload immutability on internal activity
    req1_initial = nil
    req2_initial = nil

    travel 1.minute do
      post "/api/v1/requests",
        params: { request: { subject: "Billing discrepancy", comment: { body: "Charged twice on invoice #10." } } },
        headers: account_headers("acme", avery_token),
        as: :json
      assert_response :created
      req1_initial = response.parsed_body.fetch("request")
    end

    travel 2.minutes do
      post "/api/v1/requests",
        params: { request: { subject: "Feature question", comment: { body: "Do you support webhooks?" } } },
        headers: account_headers("acme", avery_token),
        as: :json
      assert_response :created
      req2_initial = response.parsed_body.fetch("request")
    end

    t1_id = req1_initial["id"]

    # Initially unassigned on /tickets

    assert_nil response.parsed_body.dig("ticket", "assignee")

    # Cannot assign ticket to a customer or nonexistent user

    end

    travel 4.minutes do

            comment: {

    assert_equal 1, response.parsed_body["count"]
    assert_equal [ "Charged twice on invoice #10." ], response.parsed_body.fetch("comments").map { |c| c["body"] }

    post "/api/v1/invitations",

      params: { invitation: { email: "not-an-email", role: "agent" } },
      headers: account_headers("acme", acme_owner_token),
      as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    # Cancelling Acme blocks previewing and accepting invitations, /users, /invitations, /staff
    post "/api/v1/account/cancel", headers: account_headers("acme", acme_owner_token), as: :json
    assert_response :ok

    post "/api/v1/invitation_previews",

    assert_response :forbidden

    assert_not Account.exists?(acme_id)

My focus is on ensuring robust, predictable, and secure behavior across our API endpoints.

First, I'm zeroing in on the crucial `POST /api/v1/invitation_previews` and `POST /api/v1/invitation_acceptances` endpoints. The core of this is the correct handling of the `X-Helpdesk-Account` header. It's multi-tenant, so any request needs to be scoped to a particular account, or it should 404. Let's make sure the logic handles various scenarios like a missing header, an incorrect header, and the correct header. This covers cross-tenant isolation by design. This is especially important given how the frontend utilizes the subdomain. I need to guarantee that these endpoints behave as expected with and without the header, reflecting the correct account lookups and error responses (404, 422). I am checking email confirmations and password resets to ensure the multi-tenant architecture stays consistent.

Next, I'm thinking about the staff's ability to update tickets through `PATCH /api/v1/tickets/:id`. Specific attention is given to how internal comments and assignments affect customer visibility, ticket status, and timestamps. I need to confirm that private notes and no-op assignments (same assignee) do not trigger unnecessary updates for the customer, keeping the customer's view consistent.

Now, a focus on customer-facing requests via `POST /api/v1/requests` and updates. I'm verifying that customers *cannot* manipulate `assignee_id` or force a public comment. The API must strictly enforce their permitted actions and return the correct error codes.

I also need to ensure that admin updates to their own or other user profiles using `PATCH /api/v1/me` and `PATCH /api/v1/users/:id` are correctly handled. Admin rights should be scoped only to the permitted fields and ignore any unauthorized parameters. I also need to ensure that any updates to a user's name on a ticket is reflected in the correct JSON output.

I'm thinking about the potential pitfalls when suspending an account owner who's also an admin, especially when another active admin exists. There's a check that a second active admin is in place to prevent locking. There is now a check that active admins may suspend admins only who are active.

Invited emails with incorrect casing or whitespace are also reviewed, I confirm that these are all automatically normalized and will not interfere with any queries.

I check edge cases of `POST /api/v1/invitations`, specifically dealing with malformed JSON input. Missing keys, or an empty invitation object needs to be gracefully rejected.

I have implemented all requested features and verified them with integration tests and a live server check:

- **Team Invitations (`/api/v1/invitations`, `/api/v1/invitation_previews`, `/api/v1/invitation_acceptances`)**:
  - Admins can invite other `admin` or `agent` team members via `POST /api/v1/invitations`, emailing a link to `/accept-invitation?account=<subdomain>&token=<token>`.
  - Admins can list invitations ordered by ID ascending (with `status` filtering across `pending`, `accepted`, `revoked`, and `expired`), inspect individual invitations (`GET /api/v1/invitations/:id`), resend invitations (`POST /api/v1/invitations/:id/resend`), and revoke pending invitations (`DELETE /api/v1/invitations/:id`).
  - Competing pending invitations and existing account emails are rejected, and customer registration (`POST /api/v1/registrations`) cannot claim an email with a pending invitation.
  - `POST /api/v1/invitation_previews` previews the invited email, role, business name, subdomain, and expiry inside `invitation_preview`, and `POST /api/v1/invitation_acceptances` creates a verified team member who can sign in immediately without another verification email, returning `user` and `account`.
- **People Management & Staff Choices (`/api/v1/users`, `/api/v1/staff`)**:
  - Added `suspended` to users and exposed `GET /api/v1/users` (ordered by ID ascending, filterable by `role` and `suspended`), `GET /api/v1/users/:id`, and `PATCH /api/v1/users/:id` for admins only.
  - Suspending a user revokes their sessions, blocks sign-in, and clears their ticket assignments, while protecting the last active admin from suspension or demotion.
  - Added `GET /api/v1/staff` for staff (`admin` and `agent`) returning active staff choices ordered by ID ascending.
- **Ticket Assignments & Private Notes (`/api/v1/tickets`, `/api/v1/requests`)**:
  - Both admins and agents can work on tickets and assign or clear `assignee_id` (`null`), returning `assignee_id` and `assignee` (`id` and `name`) on tickets.
  - Private notes (`public: false`) are visible to staff and hidden from customers, and internal activity (private notes, assignments, and suspension-triggered unassignment) does not alter customer-facing requests or request ordering.
